figures.caption: Table 1: Empirical rejection rates for LazyVI, Logistic Regression, and DNN-Inference under linear and nonlinear signal settings.
Figure 2: Log-log plot of the sorted NTK eigenvalues. The spectrum decays faster than the red reference line with slope −1, supporting the regularity condition α > 1.
Figure 3: Representative samples of digits ‘8’ and ‘9’ from the test set. The overlay illustrates the 7× 7 pixel grid boundaries used for the fine-grained analysis. Regions are labeled from 1 to 16.

Figure 4: Heatmaps of Variable Importance (VI) across three granularity levels. Columns compare the estimation methods: Lazy Training, Dropout, and Retraining. Warmer colors indicate higher importance.

Figure 5: Heatmaps of Lazy Training p-values across three levels of granularity. The p-values are multiplied by 2, 4, or 16 for the Top vs Bottom, Quadrant, and 16-Region respectively for the Bonferroni correction with values capped at 1, then are transformed using − log10(max{0.0001, p}) to enhance visual contrast and highlight significance. A score at approximately 1.3 and above corresponds to p ≤ .05.
